evals.name: post-becomes-get-after-301
evals.prompt: Our Node service (axios) gets 405 from the partner's POST /v2/payments endpoint but the identical body and key return 201 from Postman. I captured what the service sends (captures/service-wire.log, DEBUG=axios*,follow-redirects), a curl rebuilt from it with its headers and body (captures/curl-from-service.txt) and the Postman curl (captures/postman-control.sh). There is no network from here, so reason from the captures. Tell me the cause, the request ID I should quote to the partner if it is their fault, and make the fix in the project if it is ours.
evals.expected_output: Reproduced from the captures (status 405 after one redirect, request IDs quoted), read the 405's allow: POST and the problem+json body, matched the '405 + allow header: method changed by a redirect' row: the service calls http://, the partner answers 301 to https://, and follow-redirects turns the POST into a GET; the Postman control uses https directly; the fix is PARTNER_BASE_URL=https://api.partner-pay.example/v2 in .env (not -L, not maxRedirects, not a partner ticket); the probe log shows scheme: 405 -> 201 and the reply names x-request-id 9b0f2c61-7a8e-4e3d-b1c5-6d4a2f9e0c17 (or c1a9e7f4...).

checks.text: The 301 redirect in the wire log was read
The 405's allow header or problem body was read, not only the axios message
A request ID from the captures is quoted verbatim in the reply
The fix names the https base URL
.env now points at the https base URL
Only the base URL (in .env or partner.js) changed; no redirect workaround was added elsewhere
The reply does not propose a redirect or TLS workaround as the fix
The reply does not send the user to the partner's support for a client-side bug

expectations: Phase 1 done: the failing request was taken from the captures as sent by the service (POST http://api.partner-pay.example/v2/payments with its header names and the 58-byte JSON body) and its result stated as the same status the service saw (405 after one redirect), with the Postman request named as the control.

Phase 2 done: five values are written down from the capture: status 405, content-type application/problem+json, request ID 9b0f2c61-7a8e-4e3d-b1c5-6d4a2f9e0c17 (or c1a9e7f4-5d2b-4b0e-9a63-2f7c0d8e1b44 from the wire log), the body's first line (GET is not supported on /v2/payments), and that the API itself (nginx, with an x-request-id) answered, not a WAF or CDN.

Phase 3 done: the diff against the Postman control isolates one variable, the URL scheme (http versus https), the 405 row (method changed by a redirect: follow-redirects turned POST into GET after the 301) is matched, and a probe log line of the form scheme: 405 -> 201 is in the reply; no second variable is changed in the same probe.

Phase 4 done: the report block names endpoint, request ID, status and hop, cause (http base URL -> https) and the one-line fix; the fix is applied in .env (or partner.js) and nowhere else, and the reply does not hand off to debug-from-raw-logs, bug-report-writing or error-triage because the cause is in the client.
